data.revised_prompt:
Publication-quality academic infographic, flat vector style, white background, landscape 16:9 aspect ratio, journal-ready scientific figure, not poster-like. Title at top: “Timeline of Satellite Embedding Models”. Clean typography, generous spacing, minimalist grid, crisp vector lines, restrained earth-observation palette only: deep blue, forest green, warm ochre, slate gray, with subtle tints. 

Main content: a horizontal timeline spanning 2022 to 2026 across the center-left to center of the figure. Years labeled clearly along the axis: 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026. Place model names as labeled nodes on the timeline with small callout leader lines where needed. Keep all labels legible, medium-sized, no overlap, optimized for a survey paper figure. Use compact, elegant annotation tags.

Group nodes by color-coded families with a small legend on the right side. Include legend entries with matching colors and brief family names:
- precomputed embedding products
- vision-language models
- masked autoencoder family
- multimodal generalist EO encoders
- application-specialized EO encoders

Include representative model nodes on the timeline: SatMAE, ScaleMAE, Prithvi, RemoteCLIP, SatVision, SatMAE++, DOFA, Copernicus, AnySat, Galileo, WildSAT, TerraMind, FoMo, GSE, AgriFM, TerraFM, TESSERA, THOR.

Arrange models chronologically from left to right from 2022 through 2026. Use family-based color coding and subtle grouping bands or node colors, but keep the overall appearance restrained and elegant. Suggested placement logic: earliest masked autoencoder models on left; precomputed embedding products and vision-language models around 2023; multimodal generalist encoders through 2024-2025; application-specialized EO encoders and newer models toward 2025-2026. Include subtle callout annotations near relevant clusters such as “vision-language”, “precomputed annual product”, and “multimodal generalist”.

Design constraints: flat vector graphics, no 3D, no glossy effects, no photorealism, no decorative background elements, no icons unrelated to scientific figure design, no heavy shadows. The figure should look like a polished journal infographic suitable for a review article in remote sensing / geospatial ML. All labels must be English only. Ensure the right-side legend is compact and the main timeline occupies most of the width. Use precise alignment, thin rules, and restrained use of color.
